cf.title: ON EMPTY clause for aggregate and window functions

input.subject: ON EMPTY clause for aggregate and window functions

verdict_reasoning: The proposal fails at level 1b. In message #11 the author accepts that v3 never differs from COALESCE, and message #7 covers the remaining case with a count()-based CASE (demand-1). The costs named in message #9 fall on everyone (maintenance-fit-1), the migration need names no database (demand-2), and the standard edition is not published (standards-compat-2). The list must agree that the clause is wanted, and in which form, before code review makes sense.

brief.title: ON EMPTY clause to give aggregates a value for empty input
brief.problem: An aggregate over zero rows returns NULL, and users must wrap it in COALESCE to get a different value. The author cites an upcoming SQL standard revision that defines ON EMPTY for sum() and product(), and Vik Fearing cites migration from other databases that support it.
brief.proposed_design: v1 tracked per group whether any row reached the aggregate and returned the given value only on truly empty input, which blocked partial aggregation. v2 and v3 define agg(args, default ON EMPTY) as exactly COALESCE(agg(args), default) for plain and window aggregates. A later WIP patch accepts ON EMPTY only on sum() and product() and rewrites it to COALESCE at parse time.
user_visible_surface: SQL syntax agg_function(args, default_value ON EMPTY), also with ALL, DISTINCT and before WITHIN GROUP.
ON EMPTY on aggregates used as window functions, returning the value for an empty frame (rejected in the WIP patch).
New fields in Aggref, WindowFunc and FuncCall stored in pg_rewrite, needing a catversion bump (v1 to v3).
View and rule deparse shows COALESCE in place of ON EMPTY in the WIP patch.
author_claims: ON EMPTY is expected in an upcoming SQL standard revision, defined as COALESCE over the result for SUM and PRODUCT.
v1 behaved differently for plain and windowed sum() over all-NULL input, because their transition functions differ in strictness.
The author found no case where the general v3 design differs from COALESCE, and accepts it adds little value.
The WIP patch is under 150 lines with tests, with no executor or catalog changes.
brief.thread_state: Robert Haas and Tom Lane see little value over COALESCE and object to the sum()/product()-only version, and Tom calls the parse-time rewrite an ugly hack. Vik Fearing wants a generic version or none, and no reply came after 2026-09-28.
unclear: The material does not say which version is meant for commit: v3 general or the WIP subset.
No user case is given where the v1 empty-input rule gives an answer that a count()-based CASE cannot.
The material does not say what the committer, Peter Eisentraut, thinks of the open objections.
The standard text is quoted only second-hand, and no other databases that support ON EMPTY are named.

prior_attempts.title: MAP syntax for arrays
prior_attempts.who_objected: Tom Lane, Andreas Karlsson, Ashutosh Bapat
prior_attempts.quote: Yeah, it's a handy syntax, but it's not that much better than using a subselect or a writing a user-defined function. And there's risk of future conflicts with the SQL standard.
prior_attempts.reason: Reviewers objected to adding proprietary syntax that could conflict with future SQL standard use of the MAP keyword, which is already a non-reserved keyword in SQL:2016. They also judged the syntax not much better than the existing sub-select with unnest and array_agg, which is more flexible (for example, it allows a WHERE filter), and suggested optimizing the unnest/array_agg combination in the planner instead of adding new syntax. Heikki Linnakangas summarized the consensus as not wanting the feature and marked the entry Rejected.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P9 added syntax outside the standard, while this clause comes from an expected standard edition. Both offer a new spelling for a result that an existing query form already gives.

objections.title: No user need shown beyond what COALESCE already gives
objections.failure_scenario: A user writes sum(x, 0 ON EMPTY) and gets the same result as coalesce(sum(x), 0), with no other effect. Postgres still keeps a second spelling in gram.y, ruleutils and the docs. Future aggregate work has to keep both spellings in step.
objections.argument: In message #11 the author says he found no case where v3 differs from COALESCE and will no longer argue that it adds value. Tom in message #7 shows that the one case COALESCE cannot cover, an aggregate that returns NULL for non-empty input, is handled by CASE WHEN count(x) > 0. The thread reports no user who asked for this syntax. [P9] was rejected because its syntax was not much better than an existing query form.
objections.author_must_show: Which user, query or field report needs ON EMPTY where coalesce(agg(...), value) or a count()-based CASE is not enough?

critic.reasoning: The author accepts in message #11 that v3 never differs from COALESCE, and message #7 covers the remaining case with a count()-based CASE. The only counterweights are the unpublished standard and an unnamed migration need.

objections.title: General ON EMPTY adds grammar and node upkeep for COALESCE semantics
objections.failure_scenario: Every user pays for the larger Bison grammar on each parse, and committers maintain new Aggref and WindowFunc fields, deparse code and a catversion bump. All of this produces results that users already get from COALESCE(agg(x), v).
objections.argument: Message #11 says v3 gives the same answer as COALESCE in every case the author found. Message #9 names the costs: development, maintenance and some parse-speed penalty, for a small benefit. Message #7 offers a count()-based CASE for the rare aggregate that returns NULL on non-empty input. The cost falls on everyone, and the gain is a second spelling of COALESCE.
objections.author_must_show: Which real migration or user case needs the ON EMPTY spelling instead of COALESCE, and how often does it occur?

critic.reasoning: Message #9 names grammar and maintenance costs that fall on everyone, and message #11 accepts that v3 adds no value over COALESCE. Tom calls the costs small and Robert expects the standard to outweigh them, so publication could change the balance.

objections.title: Migration demand is asserted, with no source system or users named
objections.failure_scenario: Postgres adds the grammar rule to help people port queries from other databases. If none of the usual source systems uses this spelling, nobody ports such a query. Everyone still pays the extra grammar and parsing cost Tom describes in message #9.
objections.argument: The only demand in the thread is in message #8, where Vik wants the syntax to help conversion from databases that have it. No database is named, and no migration case is shown. The standard text is quoted second-hand, and the edition is not yet published. Vik says the syntax may still change there. Message #9 says the cost falls on every parse, while the gain goes only to those who write the clause.
objections.author_must_show: Which shipping database systems accept agg(x, v ON EMPTY), and is there a migration report where its absence blocked or complicated a port to Postgres?

critic.reasoning: Message #8 is the only statement of demand, and it names no database and no migration case. Naming the systems that accept this syntax would answer it.

objections.title: Adopts draft syntax before the standard edition is published
objections.failure_scenario: Postgres 20 ships agg(x, d ON EMPTY). The published edition changes the spelling, for example to match JSON_VALUE's DEFAULT expr ON EMPTY. Postgres then carries two spellings, or users who adopted the early form find that their SQL does not port.
objections.argument: Message #8 says the next edition is not out and invites a better proposal for the syntax. Tom (message #7) and Robert (message #6) find the current spelling confusing because the substitute value looks like an aggregate argument. The same clause in SQL/JSON, which Postgres already implements, requires DEFAULT before the expression. COALESCE already gives the same result, so the risk of a future conflict is weighed against little gain, as in [P9].
objections.author_must_show: Is the ON EMPTY spelling for aggregates final in the standard draft, and why not wait for the published edition before taking it into the grammar?

critic.reasoning: Message #8 confirms the edition is not published and that the syntax could still change. Postgres already implements DEFAULT expr ON EMPTY for SQL/JSON, so a different final spelling is a concrete possibility.

other_surviving.title: General ON EMPTY uses COALESCE semantics that the name does not describe
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user writes stddev(x, -1 ON EMPTY) and gets -1 for a group that has one row. Later, the standard extends ON EMPTY to more aggregates and defines it as firing only on zero input rows. Postgres must then either break existing queries or stay incompatible with the standard.
other_surviving.argument: The standard text quoted in message #4 covers only SUM and PRODUCT, where NULL and empty input coincide. v2 and v3 apply the clause to every aggregate as a Postgres extension, so a non-empty input with a NULL result triggers it, as message #4 states for stddev and percentile_cont. v1 had the opposite rule, which shows that both readings are plausible. The project would be choosing a reading the standard has not yet made for these aggregates.
other_surviving.author_must_show: For aggregates beyond sum() and product(), why does COALESCE semantics under the name ON EMPTY match what a future standard edition will likely define?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 states that stddev(x, -1 ON EMPTY) returns -1 for one row, and presents it as a known limitation. Stating the limitation does not show that a later standard edition will define the same rule for these aggregates.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Parse-time rewrite makes views dump as COALESCE
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user creates a view that uses sum(x, 0 ON EMPTY). pg_dump and \d+ show COALESCE(sum(x), 0). A migration tool that compares the source DDL with the dumped DDL reports a difference that nobody wrote.
other_surviving.argument: The WIP patch in message #11 says that view and rule deparse shows COALESCE, while SQL-body functions keep the original text, so one feature shows two spellings. Tom (message #13) called this exposing the implementation and said the rewrite must happen later. The thread does not settle this. The brief does not say whether the WIP patch or v3 is the version proposed for commit.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Which version is meant for commit, and how does it make view deparse and pg_dump reproduce the ON EMPTY spelling the user wrote?

critic.reasoning: The WIP commit message confirms that view deparse shows COALESCE while SQL-body functions keep ON EMPTY. Tom raised this in message #13 and the thread has no answer; it applies only to the WIP patch.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: New Aggref field can be silently dropped by aggregate pushdown in postgres_fdw
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user runs `select sum(amount, 0 on empty)` on a foreign table, and postgres_fdw pushes the aggregate to the remote server. If the deparser does not know the new field, the remote query has no default, and the user gets NULL instead of 0. No error appears, and the wrong result shows up only in reports.
other_surviving.argument: v1 to v3 add an ON EMPTY field to Aggref and WindowFunc, so every piece of code that rebuilds or deparses an Aggref must learn about it. Vik found this exact silent drop in the MIN/MAX index rewrite (message #5), and message #10 fixed that one spot. The v1 file list does not touch contrib/postgres_fdw, and the v3 file list is not shown. Out-of-tree extensions that walk or copy Aggref get no compile or runtime failure when they ignore the field.
other_surviving.author_must_show: How does each consumer that deparses or rebuilds Aggref, including postgres_fdw pushdown, keep or refuse ON EMPTY, and what makes a new consumer fail loudly?

critic.reasoning: The v1 file list does not touch contrib/postgres_fdw, and message #5 shows the same silent drop already happened in the MIN/MAX path. The v3 file list is not shown, so the material cannot rule this out.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Subset version hardcodes two aggregates and exposes the rewrite in dumps
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user creates a view with sum(x, 0 ON EMPTY), and pg_dump and \d+ show COALESCE(sum(x), 0). An extension author writes a custom aggregate and finds the clause is rejected for it. A third aggregate added by a later standard needs another special case in the parser.
other_surviving.argument: Messages #12 and #13 reject a sum()/product()-only form as out of line with the project's extensibility practice. Message #13 calls the parse-time rewrite an ugly hack because view dumps expose it. Message #14 asks for a generic form or none, so the WIP patch has no supporter among the reviewers. Moving the rewrite to a later stage brings back the node fields and the upkeep that the WIP patch was meant to avoid.
other_surviving.author_must_show: How would a generic, extensible form keep ON EMPTY in deparse without the node-level upkeep that v3 carries?

critic.reasoning: Messages #12 to #14 reject the sum()/product()-only form, and no reviewer supports it. The generic v3 already exists as the alternative, so this rules out the WIP patch but not the proposal.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Syntax equivalent to COALESCE, a reason an earlier syntax proposal died
refuted.failure_scenario: Postgres ships agg(x, d ON EMPTY) as an exact alias for COALESCE(agg(x), d). Every later change to aggregate grammar, deparse and window code must then carry the extra clause, and users who move to it get nothing they could not already write.
refuted.argument: In v2 and v3 the clause is defined as COALESCE over the result (message #4), and the author found no case where the two differ (message #11). Robert Haas and Tom Lane object that it adds no value over COALESCE and costs grammar and maintenance effort (messages #6, #7, #9). That is the recorded reason [P9] was rejected, and the thread does not answer it. The only argument left is migration (message #8).
refuted.author_must_show: Which user query or migration case does ON EMPTY handle that COALESCE or a count()-based CASE cannot handle today?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1, which makes the same point without relying mainly on [P9]. [P9] was proprietary syntax at risk of conflict with the standard, while this syntax comes from a standard draft.

refuted.title: Fixing syntax before the standard text is published
refuted.failure_scenario: Postgres 20 accepts ON EMPTY on every aggregate and stores it in views. The next standard edition then changes the spelling or the meaning, for example to true empty-input semantics. Postgres is left with a non-standard form that dumped views and applications already depend on.
refuted.argument: Vik Fearing says the next edition is not out and offers to suggest better syntax (message #8), so the text may still change. The standard is quoted only second-hand (message #4). The general version also goes beyond what the standard defines for sum() and product(). [P9] records future conflict with the SQL standard as one reason it was rejected.
refuted.author_must_show: Is the ON EMPTY wording final in the next standard draft, and how would Postgres change its form if the published text differs?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which names a concrete alternative spelling the published edition could take.

refuted.title: Parse-time rewrite stores COALESCE in pg_rewrite permanently
refuted.failure_scenario: A user creates views with `sum(x, 0 on empty)` under the WIP patch, and pg_rewrite stores COALESCE(sum(x), 0). A later release adds a real ON EMPTY node, but these views keep the COALESCE form through pg_dump and pg_upgrade forever. Tools that compare view text with the source SQL report a difference for every such view.
refuted.argument: The WIP commit message says view and rule deparse shows the COALESCE rewrite, and that SQL-function bodies keep the original spelling, so the two stored forms differ. Tom objected to exposing the implementation in dumps (message #13), and the thread did not settle this. Once views exist in the rewritten form, a later design change cannot restore the user's spelling.
refuted.author_must_show: If ON EMPTY is kept as its own node later, how would views created under the parse-time rewrite be dumped, and is losing their original spelling acceptable?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-3. The stored COALESCE form gives the same results, so the added point about permanence describes no further failure.

refuted.title: Aggregate rewrites must each remember ON EMPTY, with no loud failure
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a plan shortcut that replaces an Aggref, such as another index-based rewrite like the MIN/MAX one. It does not check the ON EMPTY field. Users then get NULL instead of their stated value, and nothing signals the error until someone reports a wrong result.
refuted.argument: Message #5 found this exact silent bug: MAX(a, -1 ON EMPTY) returned NULL once an index existed. Message #10 fixed it by excluding ON EMPTY aggregates from that one path. The fix does not stop the next path that bypasses finalization from making the same mistake. COALESCE sits outside the Aggref, so it is safe from this class of bug.
refuted.author_must_show: What stops a future optimization that bypasses aggregate finalization from silently dropping ON EMPTY?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which names a concrete existing consumer of Aggref for the same class of silent drop.

refuted.title: Commits syntax before the standard edition is published
refuted.failure_scenario: Postgres ships agg(x, v ON EMPTY) with its own rules for constants, DISTINCT, window use and other aggregates. The published standard then changes the syntax or semantics. Postgres must either break stored views and applications or keep a deviating dialect forever.
refuted.argument: Message #8 says the next edition is not out and invites suggesting better syntax. Message #4 quotes the definition only second-hand, for SUM and PRODUCT only. The general version extends the syntax well beyond that text, and those extra rules are what the project would have to keep.
refuted.author_must_show: Is the ON EMPTY text final in the upcoming edition, and does it say anything about aggregates other than SUM and PRODUCT?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2. The point about extending beyond SUM and PRODUCT is covered by standards-compat-1.

refuted.title: ON EMPTY is a second spelling of COALESCE over the aggregate
refuted.failure_scenario: A user writes sum(x, 0 ON EMPTY) and gets the same result as coalesce(sum(x), 0). The project still keeps new grammar rules and their parse cost for good. In the WIP subset, a pg_dump of a view shows coalesce(...), so the user's ON EMPTY spelling is lost.
refuted.argument: Message #4 defines v2 and v3 as exactly coalesce(agg(args), default), and message #11 accepts that the general version adds no value. Tom's case when count(x) > 0 then agg(x) else v end in message #7 covers the v1 rule and lets the user choose count(x) or count(*). This leaves standard conformance and migration from other databases (message #8), but no database or user case is named. [P9] was turned down because an existing idiom did the same job.
refuted.author_must_show: Which database users are migrating from today use ON EMPTY, and what do they gain over a mechanical rewrite to coalesce()?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1. Its migration point is covered by demand-2 and its view dump point by standards-compat-3.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: v1 to v3 add fields to Aggref and WindowFunc that are stored in pg_rewrite, which needs a catversion bump.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: New fields in Aggref, WindowFunc and FuncCall affect extensions that walk, copy or deparse these nodes.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: New agg(args, value ON EMPTY) syntax taken from an unpublished standard edition, and extended beyond sum() and product().

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: v1 marks ON EMPTY aggregates non-partial, and message #10 excludes them from the MIN/MAX index path.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: The WIP patch deparses views as COALESCE, while v1 to v3 add ON EMPTY deparse in ruleutils.c.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A second spelling of COALESCE must be kept in gram.y, node fields, ruleutils.c and every code path that rebuilds an Aggref.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Message #9 names a parse-speed cost from the larger grammar, and v1 adds an executor expression step with JIT support.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: COALESCE(agg(x), v) and a count()-based CASE already give every result the proposal offers.

questions: Which user query, field report or migration case needs ON EMPTY where coalesce(agg(...), value) or a count()-based CASE is not enough?
Which shipping database systems accept agg(x, v ON EMPTY), and is there a report where its absence complicated a port to Postgres?
Is the ON EMPTY spelling for aggregates final in the standard draft, and why not wait for the published edition before adding it to the grammar?
Which version is proposed for commit, the general v3 or the WIP patch limited to sum() and product()?
For aggregates other than sum() and product(), why would a later standard edition define ON EMPTY with COALESCE semantics and not the v1 empty-input rule?

committability.owner_note: A committer is registered on the CommitFest entry but has not answered the open objections. Tom Lane and Robert Haas take part in the thread, and both object.
committability.liability: The owner signs for new aggregate grammar and, in v3, new Aggref and WindowFunc fields that every later Aggref rewrite or deparse path must handle. If the published standard differs, the owner also keeps a deviating spelling in stored views.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2, v3, a fix in message #10 and the WIP patch in message #11. The thread has no reply after 2026-09-28.

not_now.evidence_that_would_change_it: A published standard edition that fixes this spelling and its semantics, or named database systems that accept agg(x, v ON EMPTY) together with a migration report where its absence was a problem. A user case that COALESCE and a count()-based CASE cannot express would also change the answer.

priority.reason: The thread names no user or source database that needs the clause, and the standard edition it follows is not published. The general version touches grammar, node fields, planner, executor and deparse for results COALESCE already gives, so waiting for the published text costs little.

provisional_note: The code was not read, and the v3 file list is not shown. Whether postgres_fdw and other code that rebuilds or deparses Aggref keep the ON EMPTY field could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Partial aggregates push down
precedents_retrieved.summary: postgres_fdw pushes partial aggregation to the remote server for aggregates marked safe by a new pg_aggregate flag (set for min/max/sum/count). For aggregates with internal state, a new converter function runs locally and turns the remote aggregate result into the local partial-aggregate state.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tomas Vondra was still not convinced of the approach in the last review. He saw no clear path to aggregates with complex states such as avg(), and he doubted that the aggpartialpushdownsafe flag without version checks ensures the remote node represents the state the same way. The author agreed he did not know how to handle complex states, and postgres_fdw has no way to learn the remote server version at planning time. The visible messages do not show further discussion before the entry was returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
1) It's not clear to me how could this get extended to aggregates with
more complex aggregate states, to support e.g. avg() and similar fairly
common aggregates.

precedents_retrieved.title: onlyvalue aggregate
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a core aggregate function (initially named "onlyvalue", later discussed as "single_value" or "unique_value") that returns the single value present in its input group and raises an error if the group contains more than one distinct value. It is meant as a self-checking, self-documenting replacement for using min() or max() on columns expected to be constant within a group.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Dean Rasheed's review of v2 found bugs (a server crash in null handling, a cache lookup failure with complex types) and asked for more comments, a change to the finalfn call order and collation handling. The author did not post a new version for more than a month, so the commitfest manager marked the patch returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There is a review, but no input from the author for more than 1 month,
hence patch has been marked as "returned with feedback".

precedents_retrieved.title: Partial aggregates push down
precedents_retrieved.summary: Let postgres_fdw push partial aggregation down to remote servers, so each shard computes a partial aggregate state and the local server finalizes it. Early versions handled simple aggregates such as count, min, max and sum, and later versions extended this to aggregates with internal states, using added partial aggregate functions and a remote version check.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas said two major areas of work remained before the feature could be committed. Approach #2, which does the pushdown with an SQL keyword instead of separate partial aggregate functions for each aggregate, still needed investigation. Sending serialized bytea states between servers that cannot fully trust each other also needed design work and consensus. The entry closed as returned with feedback because, as vignesh C wrote, there was "still some work" left.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In addition, the problems around transmitting serialized bytea blobs between machines that can't be assumed to fully trust each other will need to be addressed in some way, which seems like it will require a good deal of design work, forming some kind of consensus, and then implementation work to follow.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add SQL syntax check
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a --syntax option to the postgres server binary that reads SQL from standard input, runs it through the raw parser only (no catalog access or parse analysis), and reports whether it is valid SQL via a message and exit code. The intent was to support manual and automated script checks and editor integrations.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Several reviewers held that the feature did not belong in the postgres binary, and Robert Haas marked the entry Rejected on that basis. The main objection, attributed to Tom Lane and endorsed by Robert Haas, was that the check exposes an implementation detail, the division of work between gram.y (raw_parser) and parse analysis, so it would miss things users consider syntax errors and flag things that seem semantic. Making that work would need a much larger effort and a different design. Robert Haas also noted that the 45-line patch had no comments, tests or documentation, and the author agreed to the rejection.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I strongly suspect that doing something useful in this area requires
about two orders of magnitude more code than are included in this
patch, and a completely different design.

precedents_retrieved.summary: empty

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Enable fast default for domains with non-volatile constraints"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Enable fast default for domains with non-volatile constraints"
Reverted commit(s): Enable fast default for domains with non-volatile constraints; Silence compiler warning from older compilers.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit a0b6ef29a51818a4073a5f390ed10ef6453d5c11, along with
its follow-up 2e123e3c2bd34f2377212a4e7cfcdbf9e2d9c7ff ("Silence compiler
warning from older compilers"), which only adjusted code introduced by

The change failed with an empty table and an invalid default, and the
best way to deal with that will involve an addition to the TAM API, so
it's not ready for relese 19 now.

precedents_retrieved.title: window function improvements WIP
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch first allowed DISTINCT inside aggregates used as window functions, such as array_agg(DISTINCT week) over a frame, with code limited to int, float and numeric. After review the author stopped that work and posted a different patch that adds RESPECT/IGNORE NULLS to lag(), lead(), first_value(), last_value() and nth_value(), with negative positions in nth_value() to read the frame in reverse.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane asked whether DISTINCT on a window function is well defined, given one output row per input row and order sensitivity. He also objected to datatype-specific code, so the author suspended the DISTINCT work. Surafel Temesgen's review of the null treatment patch found white space errors, uncommented functions, oversized regression tests and an unexplained change to makeBoolAConst. The author then judged Vik Fearing's competing <null treatment> patch the better design and offered to withdraw his own, and Michael Paquier closed the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think that Vik Fearing's patch about "Implement <null treatment> for window functions" is much clear, better and has a chance to be committed.

precedents_retrieved.title: Partial aggregates push down
precedents_retrieved.summary: Push partial aggregation down to remote servers through postgres_fdw, so each shard computes a partial aggregate state and the local server combines and finalizes the states. The first version allowed only simple aggregates such as count, max, min and sum, chosen by name, and later work tried to extend it to aggregates with an internal state type, such as avg.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages show no agreed method for sending partial states of aggregates with an internal state type, such as avg(bigint), avg(numeric) or avg(interval). The thread compared new export functions, new data types such as int128, and a record built from a list of type OIDs. Tomas Vondra said serial/deserial functions are not stable across releases. He also said that limiting pushdown to the same minor version would block it during node-by-node upgrades. The visible messages contain no closing message, and Bruce Momjian wrote that the docs were on hold until a transfer method was chosen.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: For serial/deserial we make no guarantees, it can change even in a minor release. But here we need something stable even for major releases, to allow pushdown when querying older server.

precedents_retrieved.title: MAP syntax for arrays
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Andreas Karlsson, Ashutosh Bapat
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a new expression type and syntax MAP(<func_name> OVER <array_expression>) that applies a function to each element of an array and returns the resulting array, reusing the existing array-coercion infrastructure. The author also considered a more general form mapping an arbitrary expression over an array, and reported better performance than the unnest/array_agg subquery approach for small arrays.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers objected to adding proprietary syntax that could conflict with future SQL standard use of the MAP keyword, which is already a non-reserved keyword in SQL:2016. They also judged the syntax not much better than the existing sub-select with unnest and array_agg, which is more flexible (for example, it allows a WHERE filter), and suggested optimizing the unnest/array_agg combination in the planner instead of adding new syntax. Heikki Linnakangas summarized the consensus as not wanting the feature and marked the entry Rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Yeah, it's a
handy syntax, but it's not that much better than using a subselect or a
writing a user-defined function. And there's risk of future conflicts
with the SQL standard.

precedents_retrieved.title: Push down aggregates below joins.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves aggregate planning from grouping_planner() into scan/join planning, so the planner can build a grouped RelOptInfo for each scan or join rel and place the Agg node below a join. Antonin Houska's related patch, merged into the same discussion, also supports splitting into a partial aggregate below the join and a final aggregate above it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was returned because it waited for a new version from its author for about two months. The last posted version was incomplete: it did not yet check whether a join duplicates grouping keys, it failed on cases such as grouping by a column derived through an equivalence class, and it did not handle binary equality of grouping keys. Earlier, Peter Eisentraut reported merge conflicts, partition_aggregate test failures and a missing expected output file.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch has been waiting for input from its author for a couple of
months now, so I am switching it to "Returned with Feedback".

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Change default value of default_toast_compression to "lz4""
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Change default value of default_toast_compression to "lz4""
Reverted commit(s): Change default value of default_toast_compression to "lz4", when available
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 7c1849311e49, due to the fact that more than 60% of
the buildfarm members do not have lz4 installed.  As we are in the last
commit fest of the development cycle, and that it could take a couple
of weeks to stabilize things, this change is reverted for now.

This commit will be reworked in a lighter version, as
default_toast_compression's default can be changed to "lz4" without the
switch from --with-lz4 to --without-lz4.  This approach will keep the
buildfarm at bay, and still allow builds to take advantage of LZ4 in
TOAST by default, as long as the code is compiled with LZ4 support.

A harder requirement based on LZ4 should be achievable at some point,
but it is going to require some work from the buildfarm owners first.
Perhaps this part could be revisited at the beginning of the next
development cycle.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
Reverted commit(s): Ensure that RowExprs and whole-row Vars produce the expected column names.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
In commit bf7ca1587, I had the bright idea that we could make the
result of a whole-row Var (that is, foo.*) track any column aliases
that had been applied to the FROM entry the Var refers to.  However,
that's not terribly logically consistent, because now the output of
the Var is no longer of the named composite type that the Var claims
to emit.  bf7ca1587 tried to handle that by changing the output
tuple values to be labeled with a blessed RECORD type, but that's
really pretty disastrous: we can wind up storing such tuples onto
disk, whereupon they're not readable by other sessions.

The only practical fix I can see is to give up on what bf7ca1587
tried to do, and say that the column names of tuples produced by
a whole-row Var are always those of the underlying named composite
type, query aliases or no.  While this introduces some inconsistencies,
it removes others, so it's not that awful in the abstract.  What *is*
kind of awful is to make such a behavioral change in a back-patched
bug fix.  But corrupt data is worse, so back-patched it will be.

(A workaround available to anyone who's unhappy about this is to
introduce an extra level of sub-SELECT, so that the whole-row Var is
referring to the sub-SELECT's output and not to a named table type.
Then the Var is of type RECORD to begin with and there's no issue.)

Per report from Miles Delahunty.  The faulty commit dates to 9.5,
so back-patch to all supported branches.

roaster_notes.note: Message #4 points to an earlier PRODUCT() thread where the standard's COALESCE definition was quoted. The material does not show how that thread ended.
Three objections are raised, so no note is needed.
The v1 to v3 catversion bump is routine, and pg_upgrade restores views from SQL, so old clusters are not at risk. The proposal has no WAL, standby, or wire protocol effect.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. ON EMPTY only substitutes a value for a NULL aggregate result, which any user can already do with COALESCE, and the material shows no new privileges, catalogs, maintenance-command execution paths, information channels or unbounded resource use.
Objections found; committer Peter Eisentraut has not commented on them in the visible thread.
One objection from this angle. Existing coalesce() and case with count() already give every result the proposal offers.
Two demand objections are raised. The thread shows no field reports or independent user requests, so the fitting outcome is 'not now, show demand'.
